title: How a live stream reaches you | ACME TV
description: Follow an ACME TV live stream from the cameras at the event, through the production switcher and the encoder, out over the internet to people watching at home.

hero.label: How a live stream reaches you
headline: From the event
to your screen
hero.text: A live stream passes through a few hands and a few machines before it reaches you. Here is the path the picture takes, one step at a time.

scenes.title: Cameras around the venue
scenes.text: Camera operators at different spots around the venue each follow the action from their own angle. Every camera sends its picture to the control room.

scenes.title: The production switcher
scenes.text: In the control room, the switcher operator sees every camera at once and chooses which picture goes out live. Replays and on-screen graphics are added here too.

scenes.title: The encoder
scenes.text: The finished program leaves the switcher as one video signal. The encoder compresses it into a stream small enough to send over the internet.

scenes.title: The stream
scenes.text: The stream travels over the internet to the services that carry it. They make a copy for everyone who presses play, wherever they are.

scenes.title: People watching at home
scenes.text: A few seconds later, the picture reaches TVs, phones and laptops at home, on whichever service you watch.

sections.title: A small live crew
paragraphs: ACME TV is a made-up channel used to show how this site template works. Replace this text with a few lines about your own crew and what you stream.

items.title: Your channel

items.title: Video platform
items.text: Add a link to your channel page on a video platform.

items.title: Social page
items.text: Add a link to the page where you post live.

items.q: Why does the stream run a little behind the live action?
items.a: Every step adds a little time: switching, encoding and carrying the stream across the internet. A short delay is normal for any live stream.

items.q: What does the switcher operator do?
items.a: They watch every camera at once and choose which picture you see, cutting between angles as the action develops.

items.q: Can I watch on my phone?
items.a: Yes. Most streaming services play in their phone apps and in a phone's web browser.
